title: Meet Dr Girish A C: Plastic and Cosmetic Surgery Care in Bengaluru
intro: Choosing a plastic or cosmetic surgeon is an important medical decision. Patients often want to understand a doctor’s qualifications, areas of practice and approach to consultation before considering a procedure. Dr Girish A C is associated with Curls & Curves Cosmetic Surgery Centre in Bengaluru, where people explore options for cosmetic and reconstructive concerns.
alt: Two chairs beside a clipboard in a sunlit consultation room.

sections.heading: A background in surgical training
paragraphs: According to the professional profile information supplied for this article, Dr Girish A C completed his MBBS at JJM Medical College, Davanagere; MS in General Surgery at JN Medical College, Belgaum; and MCh in Plastic Surgery at Bangalore Medical College & Research Institute. This sequence reflects training in medicine, general surgery and the specialist discipline of plastic surgery. Patients should confirm current credentials and registration details directly with the clinic or appropriate medical register.

sections.heading: Understanding the scope of plastic surgery
paragraphs: Plastic surgery includes both reconstructive and aesthetic procedures. Reconstructive care aims to restore form or function following an injury, illness, congenital difference or other condition. Cosmetic surgery focuses primarily on changes to appearance. In either setting, a responsible assessment considers medical history, desired outcomes, limitations, recovery and potential risks.

sections.heading: Areas patients commonly ask about
paragraphs: Public profiles supplied as references mention hair transplantation, nose surgery, liposuction, breast procedures, gynecomastia surgery, facelifts and scar revision among topics associated with Dr Girish A C. Availability, indications and the operating setting for each procedure should be checked with the clinic rather than assumed from online listings.

sections.heading: What to discuss at a consultation
paragraphs: A useful consultation starts with your concern and expectations. Ask whether you are a suitable candidate, what non-surgical or surgical alternatives exist, where the procedure would be performed, which risks apply to you and how follow-up care is arranged. Before-and-after images may help explain possibilities, but they cannot guarantee an individual result.

sections.heading: Making an informed decision
paragraphs: The best starting point is clear information, not a promise of dramatic transformation. Curls & Curves encourages prospective patients to discuss their concerns with a qualified clinician and understand the treatment plan before making a decision.

sections.heading: Book a consultation
paragraphs: To ask about a consultation, visit the official Curls & Curves website and confirm the clinic location and appointment details.

title: Hair Transplant in Bengaluru: Understanding FUE, FUT and Recovery
intro: Hair loss can affect confidence, but not every type of hair loss requires surgery. For people considering hair transplantation in Bengaluru, the first step is identifying the likely cause and understanding the available options. A hair transplant redistributes existing follicles from a donor area to another part of the scalp; it does not create new hair follicles.
alt: A clinician parts a man’s hair to examine thinning at the crown.

sections.heading: When is transplantation considered?
paragraphs: Hair transplantation may be appropriate for selected people with pattern hair loss and sufficient donor hair. The decision depends on age, hair-loss stability, scalp health, donor density, family history, medical conditions and expectations. Sudden hair loss or patchy shedding may require investigation rather than transplantation.

sections.heading: FUE and FUT: the difference
paragraphs: Follicular Unit Extraction (FUE) involves removing follicular units individually from the donor region. Follicular Unit Transplantation (FUT), sometimes called the strip method, removes a narrow strip of donor scalp from which follicular units are prepared. Both approaches have trade-offs related to scarring, harvesting, donor management and surgical planning. A surgeon should explain why one approach may be more suitable for a specific patient.

sections.heading: What happens during recovery?
paragraphs: Following surgery, patients may experience temporary tenderness, swelling, redness and scabbing. Transplanted hair shafts often shed before new hair growth becomes noticeable. Growth occurs over months rather than days, and the final appearance may take around a year or longer to assess. Postoperative instructions and follow-up are important.

sections.heading: Risks and limitations to understand
paragraphs: Potential problems include infection, bleeding, visible scarring, unnatural hairline design, poor graft survival or dissatisfaction with density. Existing non-transplanted hair can continue to thin. Some people may benefit from medication or other medical treatments alongside, or instead of, surgery.

sections.heading: Questions to ask your surgeon
paragraphs: Ask about the cause of your hair loss, expected donor-hair availability, who performs each part of the procedure, realistic density, future hair loss, expected downtime and total costs. Avoid promises of guaranteed growth or identical results for everyone.

sections.heading: Book a consultation
paragraphs: Considering hair restoration? Arrange an assessment to discuss whether non-surgical treatment or a transplant is appropriate for you.

title: Gynecomastia Surgery in Bengaluru: Causes, Options and Recovery
intro: Gynecomastia refers to enlargement of glandular breast tissue in males. It can occur at different ages and may be associated with hormonal changes, certain medicines or underlying health conditions. Chest fullness can also be caused primarily by fat, which is not the same as true glandular gynecomastia. An examination is important before deciding whether any procedure is appropriate.
alt: A seated man gestures toward his chest while speaking with a clinician.

sections.heading: What can cause male chest enlargement?
paragraphs: Puberty-related hormonal changes are one cause, and some cases improve without surgery. Medicines, anabolic steroids, alcohol or certain illnesses may also contribute. A doctor may review medication history, symptoms and, where indicated, order investigations to identify a treatable cause. New, painful, one-sided or rapidly changing enlargement should be assessed promptly.

sections.heading: Can gynecomastia be treated without surgery?
paragraphs: Management depends on the cause, duration and symptoms. Observation may be suitable in selected cases, particularly during adolescence. Addressing an underlying condition or medication issue may help some patients. Lifestyle changes can reduce overall fat but usually do not eliminate established glandular tissue.

sections.heading: When might surgery be considered?
paragraphs: For persistent cases that cause distress or discomfort, a surgeon may discuss removal of glandular tissue, liposuction for associated fat, or a combination. The method depends on chest anatomy, skin quality and the degree of enlargement. Surgery is not the right choice for everyone.

sections.heading: Recovery and possible complications
paragraphs: Bruising, swelling, soreness and temporary changes in sensation can occur. A compression garment may be recommended as part of a postoperative plan. Recovery and return to exercise vary. Potential complications include bleeding, infection, fluid collection, asymmetry, contour changes and scarring.

sections.heading: Preparing for a consultation
paragraphs: Discuss your symptoms, previous health conditions, medicines and goals. Ask what type of tissue is involved, whether investigations are needed, the proposed technique, recovery restrictions, where surgery will take place and what results are realistic.

sections.heading: Book a consultation
paragraphs: For concerns about male chest enlargement, seek an individual medical assessment rather than relying on online self-diagnosis.

title: Liposuction in Bengaluru: Body Contouring, Not a Weight-Loss Shortcut
intro: Liposuction is a surgical body-contouring procedure used to remove selected deposits of fat from beneath the skin. It may change the shape of a particular area, but it is not designed to treat obesity or replace medically indicated weight-management care. Understanding this distinction is one of the most important parts of an informed consultation.
alt: A sculpted torso and measuring tape on a table.

sections.heading: What does liposuction actually do?
paragraphs: A surgeon uses a cannula to remove fat from selected areas, commonly discussed in relation to the abdomen, flanks, thighs or other regions. The amount and location of removal depend on anatomy and safety considerations. Liposuction does not remove visceral fat located around internal organs and does not prevent future weight gain.

sections.heading: Who may be considered?
paragraphs: Assessment takes account of general health, body weight stability, skin elasticity, medical history, the treatment area and expectations. People with significant loose skin may need a different approach if they want to address skin excess rather than fat volume alone.

sections.heading: What happens during recovery?
paragraphs: Bruising, swelling, tenderness and temporary changes in sensation are common after surgery. Compression garments may be prescribed, and time away from work or physical activity varies with the extent of the operation. Contours typically change as swelling subsides over weeks and months.

sections.heading: What are the risks?
paragraphs: Potential complications include infection, bleeding, fluid accumulation, contour irregularities, numbness, blood clots and complications related to anaesthesia. Serious complications are uncommon but possible. The clinical setting, patient selection and aftercare matter.

sections.heading: Questions worth asking
paragraphs: Ask whether liposuction addresses your actual concern, what alternatives exist, what anaesthesia is proposed, how many areas are involved and what the complete recovery plan entails. Be cautious of advertisements that promise “instant” results or guarantee a particular appearance.

sections.heading: Book a consultation
paragraphs: Discuss your body-contouring goals with a qualified clinician to understand realistic options and whether surgery is appropriate.

title: Rhinoplasty vs Septoplasty: Understanding Two Different Nose Procedures
intro: People searching for nose surgery often encounter the terms rhinoplasty and septoplasty. Although the procedures may sometimes be combined, they have different primary goals. Rhinoplasty usually involves reshaping aspects of the nose, while septoplasty is generally performed to correct a deviated nasal septum when it contributes to breathing problems.
alt: Side profile of a woman’s face showing the bridge and tip of her nose.

sections.heading: What is rhinoplasty?
paragraphs: Rhinoplasty involves changing the shape or structure of the nose. Patients may ask about the bridge, tip, symmetry or changes following an injury. A thorough discussion should consider facial proportions, nasal anatomy, skin characteristics and how any planned change could affect airflow.

sections.heading: What is septoplasty?
paragraphs: The septum is the internal wall that separates the nasal passages. When a deviated septum contributes to breathing difficulty, septoplasty may be considered after appropriate evaluation. Not every deviated septum needs an operation, and nasal obstruction can have other causes that require different treatments.

sections.heading: Can the two procedures be combined?
paragraphs: In selected cases, a surgeon may recommend a combined functional and aesthetic approach. Such planning requires careful examination and clear separation of medical indications from personal cosmetic goals. Insurance or payment arrangements may differ between functional and cosmetic components.

sections.heading: What recovery can involve
paragraphs: Swelling, bruising, nasal congestion and temporary discomfort can occur after nose surgery. A splint or internal support may be used depending on the procedure. Visible swelling often improves earlier than the final shape, which can continue to change over many months.

sections.heading: Deciding safely
paragraphs: Ask what problem is being treated, whether non-surgical management is appropriate, what changes are realistically achievable and which risks apply. Potential complications can include bleeding, infection, persistent obstruction, asymmetry or a need for further surgery.

sections.heading: Book a consultation
paragraphs: If you are considering surgery for nasal appearance or breathing, seek an assessment that addresses both function and expectations.

seoTitle: Rhinoplasty vs Septoplasty in Bengaluru: Key Facts
description: Rhinoplasty and septoplasty serve different goals. Learn about appearance, breathing, surgical planning, recovery and questions for a nose-surgery consultation.

title: Breast Augmentation and Breast Reduction: Different Goals, Important Decisions
intro: Breast augmentation and breast reduction are different surgical procedures, even though both relate to breast size and shape. People considering either option should understand the medical indications, expected changes, alternatives and possible complications. A consultation should focus on individual needs rather than a standardised appearance.
alt: A woman talks with a clinician beside a breast implant sample.

sections.heading: What is breast augmentation?
paragraphs: Breast augmentation may involve implants or, in selected cases, fat transfer to increase or modify breast volume. Implant choices require discussion of type, placement, expected appearance, maintenance and long-term monitoring. Breast implants are not lifetime devices, and additional operations may be needed.

sections.heading: What is breast reduction?
paragraphs: Breast reduction removes some breast tissue, fat and skin to reduce breast size. For some patients, the aim may include relief from symptoms such as back, neck or shoulder discomfort. Eligibility, expected symptom improvement and potential effect on sensation or breastfeeding should be discussed individually.

sections.heading: How is the right procedure selected?
paragraphs: A surgeon considers goals, anatomy, skin quality, general health, pregnancy or breastfeeding plans and personal preferences. In some cases, a breast lift may be discussed separately or alongside another procedure. Not all concerns are best managed surgically.

sections.heading: Recovery and complications
paragraphs: Recovery can involve swelling, discomfort, restrictions on lifting and activity, and follow-up appointments. Risks may include infection, bleeding, changes in nipple sensation, asymmetry, scarring and difficulties with wound healing. Implant-specific complications can include capsular contracture, rupture and other implant-related concerns.

sections.heading: Questions before deciding
paragraphs: Ask about the expected result, incision location, scar pattern, anaesthesia, medical facility, breast imaging where relevant, long-term follow-up and the possibility of future procedures. Request information about risks in clear language and take time to consider the options.

sections.heading: Book a consultation
paragraphs: If you are exploring breast surgery, arrange a detailed consultation and seek personalised information before making a decision.

description: A balanced guide to breast augmentation and reduction: different goals, medical considerations, implant-related questions, recovery and surgical risks.
